rules.statement: Every brain must declare capabilities, allowed actions, and blocked actions.
All brains operate in approval-required mode for write-affecting outcomes.
Brain outputs must be reviewable and traceable in reports.
A brain may report execution success only when a real artifact or command result is supported by verifiable evidence.
Test execution requires explicit in-workspace targets, bounded timeouts, shell-disabled invocation, and captured exit evidence.
Engineering intelligence providers may propose bounded artifacts but may not write source, execute commands, perform Git actions, or bypass isolated Tester Brain validation and Founder approval.
Reviewer Brain approval is a technical verdict only and never authorizes source application, commit, push, deploy, or replacement of Founder approval.
Architect Brain plans are read-only and may hand off only allow-listed structured specifications; plans never authorize implementation or external action.
Correction loops are attempt-bounded, stop immediately on Reviewer rejection, accept only allow-listed structured revisions, and never authorize source or Git actions.
Revenue execution missions require an approved GARUDA-deliverable candidate, complete verification, a currently verified commercial capability, and bounded scope before Engineering begins.

Revenue work packages run through the governed Architect, Engineering, Tester, and Reviewer evidence chain; a technical result remains a Founder review checkpoint and never authorizes source, Git, deployment, outreach, contract, spending, payment, or delivery actions.
